claim: AAAI's official Main Track review criteria explicitly prefer papers whose contribution is of interest beyond a single sub-area of AI over papers that advance the state of the art only incrementally or only within a narrow sub-area.
stance_target: narrow single-domain (code-only) calibration work is disadvantaged relative to cross-cutting contributions at AAAI
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track official Call for Papers, Review Criteria section
quoted_support: Solid technical papers that explore new territory or point out new directions for research, introduce new problems, address research questions, or introduce methods that are of interest beyond a single sub-area of AI are preferred to papers that advance the state of the art, but only incrementally, or only within a narrow sub-area of AI.

claim: AAAI Main Track submissions are formally scored on four axes: significance and novelty of contribution, theoretical/empirical soundness of claims, relevance to the AAAI community, and clarity of exposition, plus reproducibility steps as an additional consideration.
stance_target: official scoring rubric for AAAI main track
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track Call for Papers
quoted_support: All submissions will be evaluated and scored for the significance and novelty of the contributions..., theoretical and/or empirical soundness of the claims, their relevance to the AAAI community, and clarity of exposition.

claim: AAAI describes itself as a highly selective conference and explicitly discourages submission of anything short of authors' best work.
stance_target: high competitive bar at AAAI main track
scope_conditions: AAAI-26 Main Technical Track Call for Papers
quoted_support: AAAI is a highly selective conference. Prospective authors are therefore strongly encouraged to submit only their very best work to AAAI.
